transcript:
This message comes from Schwab.
Investing with Schwab is like a hike with endless trails.
Go solo with self-directed investing, take stops along the way with trading, or choose
a guide with full-service wealth management.
Whatever trails you take, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
It's now just a matter of hours before the first polls open on midterm election day.
Millions of votes have already been cast in early and absentee voting, and President Trump
delivered his closing message at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.
NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben was there and says he spoke about the pool's troubled renovation
for more than 20 minutes.
Trump did eventually get to a more substantial message today, but then at the end he veered
back to the renovations once again.
And in fact, he basically acknowledged that he skipped over a lot of potential midterm
messaging.
We have a lot of great things planned for Washington, and I could get into the nation,
but for that you don't have enough time.
And while, yes, Trump loves doing these projects, it was still surprising to focus on them after
he's done all of these rallies around the country the last few weeks.
The Supreme Court has handed a setback to the Trump administration.
The Court has rejected a push for California to set aside thousands of mail ballots from
people the administration claims are non-citizens.
More than 140 statewide ballot measures face voters around the country, Jack Khalil from
Virginia's VPM News reports.
Abortion, rights for LGBTQ+ people, taxes, and voting are common themes of the ballot
measures.
For example, Virginians are deciding whether to protect abortion and same-sex marriage,
and to strengthen voting rights for people who are returning from incarceration.
Californians are deciding whether to levy a one-time wealth tax on billionaires.
And there's also two measures on California ballots that would negate that change.
There's an abortion ban on the ballot in Missouri, but the campaign pushing for that proposal
is focusing more on a ban on gender-affirming care for minors bundled with it.
Some states could see their constitutions change in ways that make it harder to pass
tax hikes or make it even harder to change constitutions.
For NPR News, I'm Jack Khalil in Richmond, Virginia.
Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs has declared a statewide state of emergency following heavy rain and
flooding.
Authorities and flagstaffs say two people are believed to have died as a result of major
flooding Sunday.
And Brian Heinches, of member station KNAU, reports that evacuations are in effect for
several communities.
The National Weather Service says some areas in north-central Arizona received six or more
inches of rain.
That triggered major flooding in Oak Creek, which runs through the tourist hotspot of
Sedona.
The normally placid waterway crested at more than 20,000 cubic feet per second Sunday night
and forced the evacuation of more than 100 homes.
The Arizona Department of Public Safety conducted at least half a dozen rooftop helicopter rescues
as water overtook residential and recreation areas.
Officials also ordered evacuations in the communities of Camp Verde and Cottonwood along the Verde
River, which reached more than five times its normal depth.
For NPR News, I'm Ryan Heinches in Flagstaff.
This is NPR News.
North Korea denies that it was behind last week's theft of more than six billion dollars
from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.
North Korea says U.S. allegations linking it to the heist are a gray political provocation.
The denial came through a statement from the influential sister of leader Kim Jong-un, the
FBI blamed North Korea over the weekend.
The Kennedy Center has announced its newest class of honorees include songwriter Paul
Anka, music producer David Foster, and actor Andy Garcia.
And Piers Anastasios-Yokas has more.
Several of this year's nominees publicly support President Trump and MAGA, including David
Mamet, who called Trump the "best president since Abraham Lincoln."
This year's ceremony will take place on December 7th at Washington, D.C.'s Capital One Arena.
It's the first time since the awards were established in 1978 that the honors will not
be held at the Kennedy Center.
Its main building has been closed since September after its board said the structure is unsafe
and that the center's finances were within weeks of bankruptcy.
President Trump has threatened to demolish the building if his name is not attached to
it.
A federal court case to prevent his name from being added is ongoing.
Anastasios-Yokas, NPR News.
More than 20 years after launch, NASA's Swift Observatory expected to reenter Earth's atmosphere
on Wednesday.
The observatory weighs 3,200 pounds and was designed to study some of the universe's most
powerful explosions.
NASA says most of it will burn up as it travels through the atmosphere and that components
that do survive reentry are not likely to harm anyone.
This is NPR News.
